easy.explanation: Jehoram the son of Ahab began to reign over Israel in Samaria.
easy.q: Who began to reign over Israel in Samaria?

easy.explanation: Jehoram put away the image of Baal that his father had made.
Mesha king of Moab rebelled against the king of Israel after Ahab died.
easy.q: Who rebelled against the king of Israel?

medium.explanation: Jehoram cleaved unto the sins of Jeroboam the son of Nebat.
medium.q: In what sins did Jehoram continue, even after removing the image of Baal?

medium.explanation: Jehoram went out of Samaria and numbered all Israel.
medium.q: What did Jehoram do after the king of Moab rebelled against him?

medium.explanation: In this passage, rebelled means that Moab rose up against the king of Israel.
medium.q: What does the word “rebelled” mean in the statement that the king of Moab rebelled?

answers: Jehoram made only a partial change
challenge.explanation: He removed Baal’s image but still continued in the sins of Jeroboam.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from Jehoram removing Baal’s image while continuing in Jeroboam’s sins?

challenge.explanation: Moab’s revolt led Jehoram to number Israel and prepare for war.
challenge.q: What caused Jehoram to begin military preparations?

answers: One hundred thousand lambs and one hundred thousand rams with the wool
challenge.explanation: Mesha had rendered one hundred thousand lambs and one hundred thousand rams with the wool.
challenge.q: What detail shows that Moab had supplied Israel with a large amount of produce before the revolt?

paragraphs.title: The Alliance of the Three Kings and the Lack of Water

easy.explanation: Jehoram asked Jehoshaphat king of Judah to go with him against Moab.
easy.q: From whom did Jehoram ask for help in the war?

easy.explanation: The king of Edom joined Jehoram and Jehoshaphat.
easy.q: Which other king joined the campaign?

easy.explanation: There was no water for the host and the cattle.
easy.q: What was lacking after the armies had traveled seven days?

answers: The way through the wilderness of Edom
The way along the wall of Moab
medium.explanation: They chose the way through the wilderness of Edom.
medium.q: Which route did the kings choose?

answers: The army had lost its way
There was no water for the host and cattle
The king of Edom had left
medium.explanation: The lack of water made Jehoram fear that the LORD had delivered the three kings into Moab’s hand.
medium.q: Why did the king of Israel fear defeat?

answers: I am with you and on your side
medium.explanation: Jehoshaphat agreed to join Jehoram and cooperate in the campaign.
medium.q: What did Jehoshaphat mean by saying, “I am as thou art”?

answers: A request for help, Edom joins, the journey, and a lack of water
A lack of water, the journey, a request for help, and Edom joins
Edom joins, a victory, the journey, and a lack of water
challenge.explanation: Jehoram asked Jehoshaphat for help, Edom joined, they traveled, and then they lacked water.
challenge.q: Which sequence of events is described in these verses?

answers: He fully agreed to the partnership
challenge.explanation: Jehoshaphat said, “I am as thou art, my people as thy people, and my horses as thy horses.”
challenge.q: What does Jehoshaphat’s response show about his attitude toward the alliance?

answers: Water was needed for both the army and the animals
Water was needed only for the king
The lack of water prevented the walls from being built
challenge.explanation: The passage says there was no water for the host and for the cattle.
challenge.q: Why was the lack of water especially serious?

paragraphs.title: Appeal to Elisha and the Prophecy of Water

easy.explanation: Jehoshaphat asked whether there was a prophet of the LORD through whom they could inquire of the LORD.
easy.q: Who asked whether there was a prophet of the LORD nearby?

easy.explanation: A servant of the king of Israel identified Elisha the son of Shaphat.
easy.q: Which prophet was brought before the kings?

easy.explanation: Elisha said, “But now bring me a minstrel.”
easy.q: What did Elisha ask them to bring him?

answers: Because of Jehoshaphat king of Judah
Because of the king of Moab
Because of the lack of water alone
medium.explanation: Elisha said that if he had not regarded Jehoshaphat, he would not have looked toward Jehoram.
medium.q: Why did Elisha agree to speak before the kings?

answers: It would be filled with water without wind or rain
medium.explanation: The valley would be filled with water even though they would see neither wind nor rain.
medium.q: What did Elisha say would happen in the valley?

answers: Hollows or trenches for holding water
medium.explanation: The command referred to places in the valley that could collect and hold water.
medium.q: What are “ditches” in the command to make the valley full of ditches?

answers: It caused the army to go to war
The hand of the LORD came upon Elisha afterward
challenge.explanation: When the minstrel played, the hand of the LORD came upon Elisha.
challenge.q: What role did the minstrel’s playing have in the account?

answers: The water was only an unhelpful sign
The water would supply the camp, and the LORD would also deliver Moab into their hand
The water was intended only for Moab
challenge.explanation: Elisha promised water for the people and animals as well as victory over Moab.
challenge.q: What was the connection between the need for water and the promised victory?

answers: The command to strike cities, fields, wells, and trees
The command to return to Samaria
The command to wait for rain
challenge.explanation: The prophecy included striking cities, damaging land, stopping wells, and felling trees.
challenge.q: What shows that the planned victory would include widespread damage to Moab’s land?

paragraphs.title: The Water, the Moabite Mistake, and the Victory

easy.explanation: All the Moabites heard that the kings had come up to fight against them.
easy.q: Who heard that the kings had come to fight against Moab?

easy.explanation: The Moabites saw the water as red as blood.
easy.q: How did the water appear to the Moabites?

easy.explanation: The Israelites rose up and smote the Moabites.
easy.q: What did the Israelites do when the Moabites came to the camp?

answers: They thought the kings had slain one another
They knew the water had been filled with blood
They thought the king of Edom had dyed it
medium.explanation: They thought the three kings had been slain and had smitten one another.
medium.q: Why did the Moabites think the water was red?

answers: They thought there was no water
They thought the camp was defeated and went for the spoil
They thought the kings had retreated to Judah
medium.explanation: They misunderstood the appearance of the water and went to take the spoil.
medium.q: What mistake caused the Moabites to come to the camp?

answers: Goods taken from a defeated enemy
medium.explanation: The Moabites thought they could take the possessions of the defeated camp.
medium.q: What does “spoil” mean in this passage?

answers: The water gave Moab a way of escape
The water caused Moab to make a mistake, allowing Israel to attack
The water prevented Israel from fighting
challenge.explanation: The appearance of the water deceived Moab and caused the army to come out unprepared.
challenge.q: What connection is there between the appearance of the water and Moab’s defeat?

challenge.explanation: They saw the water in the morning sunlight and imagined that it was blood.
challenge.q: What made the Moabites think that the kings had fought one another?

answers: Moab was preparing to resist the invasion
challenge.explanation: The Moabites gathered those able to bear arms and stood in the border.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from Moab standing on the border before the battle?

paragraphs.title: The Destruction of Moabite Cities and the Siege of Kir-hareseth

answers: They gave them back to Moab
easy.explanation: The armies beat down the cities of Moab.
easy.q: What did the armies do to the cities of Moab?

easy.explanation: They stopped all the wells of water.
easy.q: What did they do to the wells of water?

easy.explanation: Kir-hareseth remained, and the slingers attacked it.
easy.q: Which city remained as the principal stronghold?

answers: They cast stones on it and filled it
medium.explanation: Every man cast his stone on the good land and filled it.
medium.q: What did the armies do to every good piece of land?

medium.explanation: The armies felled all the good trees.
medium.q: What did they do to the good trees?

answers: Fighters who attacked by throwing stones
medium.explanation: The slingers were soldiers who attacked the city and its wall by casting stones.
medium.q: What were the slingers who went about Kir-hareseth?

answers: It harmed only the king of Moab
It caused widespread damage to the land and its resources
It was a ceremony of peace
challenge.explanation: The actions damaged settlements, agriculture, water sources, and trees.
challenge.q: What does the attack on the cities, land, wells, and trees show about the nature of the warfare?

answers: It was the only source of water
It was the capital of Judah
challenge.explanation: After the other cities were beaten down, the slingers attacked Kir-hareseth.
challenge.q: Why was Kir-hareseth a special target after the other cities were destroyed?

answers: Destroying cities, damaging the land, stopping wells, and felling trees
Felling trees, building cities, opening wells, and retreating
Stopping wells, making peace, destroying the wall, and crowning a king
challenge.explanation: This is the sequence of actions described in the verse.
challenge.q: What order of actions is described in the verse?

paragraphs.title: The Failed Breakthrough and the Sacrifice of Moab’s Prince

easy.explanation: The king of Moab took seven hundred men that drew swords.
easy.q: How many warriors did the king of Moab take for his attempted breakthrough?

easy.explanation: He tried to break through unto the king of Edom.
easy.q: To whom did the king of Moab try to break through?

easy.explanation: He took his eldest son and offered him for a burnt offering upon the wall.
easy.q: Whom did the king of Moab offer as a burnt offering?

answers: The seven hundred men could not break through
He could not find the king of Edom
medium.explanation: The verse says that the seven hundred men could not break through.
medium.q: Why did the king of Moab fail to break through?

answers: There was great indignation against Israel, and the armies departed
The king of Moab immediately surrendered
medium.explanation: There was great indignation against Israel, and the armies departed and returned to their own lands.
medium.q: What happened after the son was offered on the wall?

medium.explanation: Indignation means strong anger or outrage.
medium.q: What does “indignation” mean in the statement that there was great indignation against Israel?

answers: He moved from a military breakthrough to an extreme religious act
He moved from surrender to peace
He moved from retreat to an attack on Judah
challenge.explanation: After the military attempt failed, he offered his eldest son as a burnt offering.
challenge.q: How did the king of Moab’s attempts change during the battle?

answers: The armies departed and returned to their own lands
challenge.explanation: After the great indignation, the armies departed and returned to their own lands.
challenge.q: What was the final result of the campaign according to the end of the chapter?

answers: He was the eldest son who should have reigned in his father’s place
He was one of the soldiers
He was the king of Edom
challenge.explanation: The verse identifies him as the eldest son who should have reigned in his father’s stead.
challenge.q: Which detail emphasizes the status of the son who was offered?
